description: The image presents two pie charts comparing the distribution of different error types in Chinese spelling correction, as analyzed in the paper “A Coin Has Two Sides: A Novel Detector-Corrector Framework for Chinese Spelling Correction.” The left chart, titled “All Changes,” illustrates the proportions of six categories: P (light green, 50%), PW (dark green, 4%), RW (gold, 14%), a gray category (26%), N (light blue, 1%), and NW (blue, 5%). The right chart, titled “All Errors,” shows a similar breakdown: P (light green, 56%), PW (dark green, 3%), RW (gold, 6%), the gray category (29%), N (light blue, 1%), and NW (blue, 5%). Both charts use the same color-coded legend on the right, with each slice labeled with its percentage. The P category dominates in both charts, while the gray category is second largest in “All Changes” and third in “All Errors.” The N and NW categories remain small in both, and the PW category is notably smaller in “All Errors” than in “All Changes.” The visual layout suggests a comparison between all modifications made by the system (“All Changes”) and only those that constitute actual errors (“All Errors”), highlighting how the system’s corrections align with or diverge from ground-truth error types.
